understanding.goal_understanding: The goal was to complete each KA59 level by moving the selectable pieces so that every goal tile marked '+' in the semantic grid is occupied by a selectable piece at the same time, then repeating this across all levels until the game reports WIN.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Each turn controlled one currently selected piece (shown as P). MOVE actions attempted to shift that piece by one cell (3 pixels) in the chosen direction; movement could be blocked or behave unexpectedly depending on walls/boundaries, and the movement_blocked flags were only hints. If a pushable object (e.g., a block) was adjacent in the movement direction, the move could push it along while the selected piece moved. Levels with multiple selectables required using CLICK with an exact pixel-coordinate target_position matching another selectable's position (shown as S) to switch control; clicking empty space or an invalid/blocked target did nothing and still consumed steps.

understanding.goal_understanding: The goal was to complete each KA59 level by moving the selectable pieces so that every goal tile marked '+' in the semantic grid is occupied by a selectable piece at the same time, then repeating this across all levels until the game reports WIN.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Each turn controlled one currently selected piece (shown as P). MOVE actions attempted to shift that piece by one cell (3 pixels) in the chosen direction; movement could be blocked or behave unexpectedly depending on walls/boundaries, and the movement_blocked flags were only hints. If a pushable object (e.g., a block) was adjacent in the movement direction, the move could push it along while the selected piece moved. Levels with multiple selectables required using CLICK with an exact pixel-coordinate target_position matching another selectable's position (shown as S) to switch control; clicking empty space or an invalid/blocked target did nothing and still consumed steps.
